scenes.img: In a forest hermitage school, two boys sit side by side on a mat studying palm-leaf books before an old sage, laughing together. young Krishna: boy about twelve, blue skin, black curly hair tied up with one peacock feather, simple yellow dhoti, no crown. young Sudama: thin boy about twelve, shaven head with a small tuft, white dhoti. Huts and trees behind.
scenes.text: Long ago… two boys studied together in the forest school of the sage Sandipani. One was Krishna. The other… a poor brahmin boy named Sudama.

scenes.img: At night in a dark forest during a fierce storm, two boys huddle together under a tree, holding hands, bundles of firewood beside them, rain and lightning all around. young Krishna: boy about twelve, blue skin, black curly hair tied up with one peacock feather, simple yellow dhoti, no crown. young Sudama: thin boy about twelve, shaven head with a small tuft, white dhoti.
scenes.text: One day their teacher’s wife sent them to gather firewood. A storm caught them deep in the forest… and the two boys held on to each other all night, until dawn.

scenes.img: Dusk at a poor village. Sudama: thin poor brahmin man in his forties, shaven head with a small tuft of hair at the back, short grey-black beard, sandalwood tilak, sacred thread, torn white dhoti and patched white shawl, bare feet sits alone on the step of a small mud hut with a thatched roof, hands folded in prayer, eyes closed, at peace.
scenes.text: Years passed. Krishna became the king of Dwarka. Sudama stayed what he had always been… a poor, gentle man who prayed, and asked for nothing.

scenes.img: Inside a bare mud hut lit by one small lamp: empty clay pots on the floor, two thin children asleep on a mat, and Sushila, his wife: thin woman in her thirties, faded red cotton sari, kind tired face, hair in a plain bun sitting beside them, worried.
scenes.text: Some days there was not enough food in the house. His children went to sleep hungry.

scenes.img: Inside the poor hut, Sushila, his wife: thin woman in her thirties, faded red cotton sari, kind tired face, hair in a plain bun gently holds the hands of Sudama: thin poor brahmin man in his forties, shaven head with a small tuft of hair at the back, short grey-black beard, sandalwood tilak, sacred thread, torn white dhoti and patched white shawl, bare feet and speaks to him, urging him.
scenes.text: His wife said softly… Your friend Krishna is the king of Dwarka. Go to him. He will not turn you away.

scenes.img: Close view of Sudama: thin poor brahmin man in his forties, shaven head with a small tuft of hair at the back, short grey-black beard, sandalwood tilak, sacred thread, torn white dhoti and patched white shawl, bare feet looking down at his own open, empty hands, ashamed and hesitant.
scenes.text: But Sudama hesitated. How could he go to a king with empty hands? He had nothing to give.

scenes.img: Close view of the thin hands of Sushila, his wife: thin woman in her thirties, faded red cotton sari, kind tired face, hair in a plain bun tying a small handful of flattened rice into a torn piece of cloth, a little bundle.
scenes.text: So his wife borrowed four handfuls of flattened rice from the neighbours… and tied it in a torn piece of cloth.

scenes.img: Sudama: thin poor brahmin man in his forties, shaven head with a small tuft of hair at the back, short grey-black beard, sandalwood tilak, sacred thread, torn white dhoti and patched white shawl, bare feet walks alone, barefoot, along a long dusty road through dry country, a small cloth bundle tucked under his arm, the sun low.
scenes.text: Sudama walked for days, barefoot… the small bundle tucked under his arm.

scenes.img: Sudama: thin poor brahmin man in his forties, shaven head with a small tuft of hair at the back, short grey-black beard, sandalwood tilak, sacred thread, torn white dhoti and patched white shawl, bare feet, tiny, stands before the enormous golden gates of Dwarka, a shining city of palaces by the sea, with tall guards looking down at him.
scenes.text: Then he saw it. Dwarka, the golden city by the sea. Palaces. Gates. Guards. He felt very small.

scenes.img: In a golden palace hall, Krishna: blue-skinned young man, clean-shaven, long black curly hair, tall gold crown with one peacock feather, yellow silk dhoti and a jewelled royal shawl, white-and-marigold flower garland, white U-shaped tilak runs barefoot with open arms and embraces Sudama: thin poor brahmin man in his forties, shaven head with a small tuft of hair at the back, short grey-black beard, sandalwood tilak, sacred thread, torn white dhoti and patched white shawl, bare feet, holding him tight; courtiers stare in surprise.
scenes.text: But when Krishna saw him from far away… he rose and ran to him, and held his old friend in his arms.

scenes.img: Sudama: thin poor brahmin man in his forties, shaven head with a small tuft of hair at the back, short grey-black beard, sandalwood tilak, sacred thread, torn white dhoti and patched white shawl, bare feet sits on a jewelled royal seat while Krishna: blue-skinned young man, clean-shaven, long black curly hair, tall gold crown with one peacock feather, yellow silk dhoti and a jewelled royal shawl, white-and-marigold flower garland, white U-shaped tilak kneels before him and washes his dusty feet in a gold basin with his own hands, eyes full of love.
scenes.text: Krishna sat Sudama on his own seat… washed his tired feet with his own hands, and touched that water to his own head.

scenes.img: Evening in a palace room lit by lamps: Krishna: blue-skinned young man, clean-shaven, long black curly hair, tall gold crown with one peacock feather, yellow silk dhoti and a jewelled royal shawl, white-and-marigold flower garland, white U-shaped tilak and Sudama: thin poor brahmin man in his forties, shaven head with a small tuft of hair at the back, short grey-black beard, sandalwood tilak, sacred thread, torn white dhoti and patched white shawl, bare feet sit together on a cushioned couch, laughing as they talk like old friends.
scenes.text: They talked for hours. About their teacher. About that night in the storm. Like two boys again.

scenes.img: Sudama: thin poor brahmin man in his forties, shaven head with a small tuft of hair at the back, short grey-black beard, sandalwood tilak, sacred thread, torn white dhoti and patched white shawl, bare feet sits on a gold couch, embarrassed, hiding a small torn cloth bundle behind his back, surrounded by gold and silk.
scenes.text: Sudama kept the little bundle hidden. Next to all that gold… his gift felt like nothing.

scenes.img: Krishna: blue-skinned young man, clean-shaven, long black curly hair, tall gold crown with one peacock feather, yellow silk dhoti and a jewelled royal shawl, white-and-marigold flower garland, white U-shaped tilak has pulled open the small torn cloth bundle and eats a handful of flattened rice with delight, while Sudama: thin poor brahmin man in his forties, shaven head with a small tuft of hair at the back, short grey-black beard, sandalwood tilak, sacred thread, torn white dhoti and patched white shawl, bare feet watches, moved to tears.
scenes.text: But Krishna saw it. What have you brought me? He pulled the cloth open… and ate a handful of the rice, as if it were the finest food in the world.

scenes.img: Dawn. Sudama: thin poor brahmin man in his forties, shaven head with a small tuft of hair at the back, short grey-black beard, sandalwood tilak, sacred thread, torn white dhoti and patched white shawl, bare feet walks away from the golden city along the road, smiling peacefully, empty-handed, content.
scenes.text: Sudama left the next morning. He had not asked for a single thing. He was simply happy… he had seen his friend.

scenes.img: Where a poor hut stood there is now a fine house with a garden, and Sushila, his wife: thin woman in her thirties, faded red cotton sari, kind tired face, hair in a plain bun and two healthy children come running out to greet Sudama: thin poor brahmin man in his forties, shaven head with a small tuft of hair at the back, short grey-black beard, sandalwood tilak, sacred thread, torn white dhoti and patched white shawl, bare feet, who stands amazed.
scenes.text: But where his hut had stood… there was now a shining house. And his family came out to meet him, no longer hungry.

scenes.img: In a fine but simple room, Sudama: thin poor brahmin man in his forties, shaven head with a small tuft of hair at the back, short grey-black beard, sandalwood tilak, sacred thread, torn white dhoti and patched white shawl, bare feet sits on a plain mat in prayer before a small lamp and a small image of Krishna, humble and calm.
scenes.text: And Sudama? He stayed the same gentle man. He lived simply… and kept loving his friend.
Krishna had never wanted the rice. He wanted the love… it was carried in.
Krishna says in the Gita… Whoever offers me, with love, a leaf, a flower, a fruit, or a little water… I accept it.
